<Rep. Robert C. "Bobby" Scott, Rep. Suzanne Bonamici, Rep. Mark DeSaulnier, Rep. Jahana Hayes, Rep. Summer L. Lee>: • truck drivers who chart their own path on the
road in order to deliver packages;
• bartenders who manage the atmosphere of a bar
by selecting background music, decide whether to ban
unruly customers, and mix cocktails according to their
own recipes;
• chefs who are given an overall budget for
ingredients and freedom to design daily menus; and
• dietary aides in health care facilities who
customize meals for patients' specific needs.
Given the many jobs in which the exercise of discretion is just a fact of life, the bill would put workers throughout the economy at risk of losing employment and labor law protections.
Converting Jobs to Gigs
Adding to the threat is the growing trend of offering work through app-based on-demand gig platforms. On their face, gig platforms seem little different from temp firms, labor brokers, and other labor market intermediaries. Nevertheless, platforms such as Uber, Lyft, and their ilk have loomed large in discussions and debates about the future of work.\21\
\21\ See, e.g., Shao Chang, Gig Economy and the Future of Work, The Flaw (July 11, 2022), https://theflaw.org/articles/gig-economy-and-the-future-of-work-uber-lyfts-race-to-the-bottom-an-opportunity-to-redefine-work/; Dara Khosrowshahi, Logan Green & John Zimmer, Uber, Lyft Ready to Do Our Part for Drivers, S.F. Chron. (June 12, 2019), https://www.sfchronicle.com/opinion/openforum/article/Open-Forum-Uber- Lyft-ready-to-do-our-part-for-13969843.php; Brett Collins et al., Is Gig Work Replacing Traditional Employment?: Evidence from Two Decades of Tax Returns, Russell Sage Found. (Mar. 2019), https:// www.russellsage.org/reports/gig-work-replacing-traditional-employment-evidence-two-decades-tax-returns; Robert Maxim & Mark Muro, Rethinking Worker Benefits for an Economy in Flux, The Avenue (Brookings Inst.) (Mar. 30, 2018), https://www.brookings.edu/blog/the-avenue/2018/03/29/ rethinking-worker-benefits-for-an-economy-in-flux/; N.Y. Times Ed. Bd., No, Robots Aren't Killing the American Dream, N.Y. Times (Feb. 20, 2017), https://www.nytimes.com/2017/02/20/opinion/no-robots-arent-killing-the-american-dream.html.
The bill seems tailor-made to exempt on-demand platform companies from accountability. The platforms typically classify workers as independent contractors and portray themselves as mere market platforms, even though many of them set the rates to be charged; retain the right to penalize workers by expelling them from the platform; make fewer total gigs or choice gigs available for any reason; and use algorithms to distribute opportunities and benefits in order to maximize platform profits and align worker availability with the platform's needs.\22\ So long as the work itself is not directly micromanaged, the platforms could continue to exercise the full range of authority they already enjoy and, under this bill, be shielded from any employment or labor law accountability.
\22\ The Gig Trap: Algorithmic, Wage and Labor Exploitation in Platform Work in the US, Hum. Rts. Watch (May 12, 2025), https:// www.hrw.org/report/2025/05/12/the-gig-trap/ algorithmic-wage-and-labor-exploitation-in-platform-work-in-the-us; Marshall Steinbaum, The Antitrust Case Against Gig Economy Labor Platforms, LPE Proj. (Apr. 7, 2022), https://lpeproject.org/blog/the-antitrust-case-against-gig-economy-labor-platforms/.
The model is steadily expanding into occupations such as hospitality,\23\ package delivery,\24\ and even nursing.\25\ Under this bill, any reasonable amount of discretion in the work along with the ability to choose whether or not to work a gig any particular day could block workers from access to NLRA or FLSA protections, even if the affected workers have no ability to determine or negotiate their own rates of pay or are subject to a range of requirements not typically imposed by businesses on other businesses. The result is likely to be insufficient income and poor working conditions\26\ and, given the incentives to escape legal obligations simply through adopting a contract model, a shift to gig-style arrangements in other industries.
\23\See, e.g., Bartender Gig Apps That Make Finding Work Easy, ShiftNOW (Mar. 29, 2024), https://www.shiftnow.com/blog/bartender-gig-apps; FAQ Page, ShiftNOW, https://www.shiftnow.com/support/shifters (``A Shifter is an independent contractor, not an employee of ShiftNOW or the businesses on our platform. Please note that, given your independent contractor status, ShiftNOW cannot provide Shifters with proof of employment.'') (last visited May 16, 2025).
\24\See, e.g., Theo Wayt, Delivering in the Dark, Amazon's Gig Drivers Face Guns and Death, The Info. (Sept. 6, 2023), https:// www.theinformation.com/articles/delivering-in-the-dark-amazons-gig-drivers-face-guns-and-death; Alana Semuels, I Delivered Packages for Amazon and It Was a Nightmare, The Atlantic (June 25, 2018), https://www.theatlantic.com/technology/ archive/2018/06/amazon-flex-workers/563444/.
\25\See, e.g., Nursing Is Not a Side Job. Protect Patients. Reject ``Gig'' Nursing., Nat'l Nurses United, https:// www.nationalnursesunited.org/gig-nursing (last visited Oct. 14, 2023).
\26\Ben Zipperer et al., National Survey of Gig Workers Paints a Picture of Poor Working Conditions, Low Pay, Econ. Pol. Inst. (June 1, 2022), https://www.epi.org/publication/gig-worker-survey/.
DEMOCRATIC AMENDMENTS OFFERED DURING THE MARKUP
OF H.R. 1319
Committee Democrats proffered four amendments to improve the bill:
• To remedy the risks identified above that
any exercise of normal day-to-day discretion would
imperil workers' access to employment and labor
protections, one amendment would have clarified that
the exercise of discretion that is ordinary and
customary in a job does not suffice for rendering a
worker an independent contractor.
• To foster innovations in flexible work
arrangements in employment and reduce the risk that
such flexibility would be used under the bill as
evidence of independent contractor status, one
amendment would have rendered such arrangements neutral
criteria, indicative of neither independent contractor
nor employee status.
• To ensure fair application of the bill's new
test, one amendment would have enabled workers to take
any challenge over status to the courts, despite any
forced arbitration policy funneling other disputes to
private arbitration.
• Finally, given that any change to FLSA's
employment coverage alters the boundaries of child
labor rules, one amendment would have excluded child
labor provisions from the bill's new test.

CONCLUSION
For the reasons stated above, Committee Democrats unanimously opposed H.R. 1319 when the Committee on Education and Workforce considered it on July 23, 2025. We urge the House of Representatives to do the same.
Robert C. ``Bobby'' Scott,
Ranking Member.
